question: Which of the following best defines normal labour (eutocia)?

options.A: Surgical delivery via lower segment cesarean section at 36 weeks
options.B: Spontaneous onset, vertex presentation, term gestation, and uncomplicated delivery
options.C: Induced labour with breech presentation at 34 weeks gestation
options.D: Prolonged labour requiring extensive instrumental assistance

explanation: Normal labour is characterized by a spontaneous onset, vertex presentation, term gestation, and absence of complications for mother and baby. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T005#GNS226_U3_T005_h1)

question: What is the primary role of the nurse during the initial phase of normal labour?

options.C: Providing support, monitoring vital signs, and assessing contractions

explanation: Nurses support the mother psychologically and physically by monitoring vital signs and contraction patterns while watching for any deviations from normal progress. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T005#GNS226_U3_T005_h1)

question: What do the 'four Ps' of labour represent?
explanation: The four Ps of labour stand for Power, Passage, Passenger, and Psyche, which are the fundamental prerequisites for normal childbirth. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T005#GNS226_U3_T005_h2)

question: What is the main purpose of the cardinal features of labour?

options.A: To measure the exact volume of amniotic fluid
options.B: To ensure the smallest diameter of the fetal head navigates the birth canal
options.C: To stimulate the release of oxytocin from the posterior pituitary

explanation: The cardinal movements are specific adjustments the fetus makes so that its smallest head diameters can successfully pass through the maternal pelvis. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T005#GNS226_U3_T005_h2)

question: What anatomical landmark defines when engagement of the fetal head has occurred?

options.A: When the biparietal diameter reaches or passes below the pelvic inlet / ischial spines
options.B: When the anterior fontanelle touches the perineum
options.C: When the mentum reaches the coccyx
options.D: When the sagittal suture aligns with the sacral promontory

explanation: Engagement is defined as the passage of the widest transverse diameter of the fetal head (biparietal diameter) to or below the pelvic inlet. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T005#GNS226_U3_T005_h3)

question: Which of the following is a primary force driving fetal descent during labour?

options.A: Passive stretching of the broad ligament
options.B: Uterine contractions and maternal pushing efforts

explanation: Descent is driven by uterine contractions, amniotic fluid pressure, maternal pushing, and the straightening of the fetal body axis. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T005#GNS226_U3_T005_h3)

question: What is the primary mechanical advantage of fetal head flexion?

options.A: It increases the heart rate of the fetus
options.B: It replaces a larger diameter with a smaller suboccipito-bregmatic diameter
options.C: It prevents meconium staining of the amniotic fluid
options.D: It initiates the third stage of labour

explanation: Flexion forces the chin to the chest, replacing the longer occipitofrontal diameter with the smaller suboccipito-bregmatic diameter for easier passage. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T005#GNS226_U3_T005_h4)

question: What part of the fetal head becomes the leading landmark during proper flexion?
explanation: With proper flexion, the occiput becomes the dependent and leading part felt during vaginal examinations. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T005#GNS226_U3_T005_h4)

question: What anatomical structure primarily guides the internal rotation of the fetal head?

options.B: The levator ani muscles of the pelvic floor

explanation: The sloping muscles of the pelvic floor, particularly the levator ani, act as a slide that directs the fetal head to rotate anteriorly. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T005#GNS226_U3_T005_h5)

question: In a normal vertex presentation, toward which maternal structure does the occiput usually rotate internally?
explanation: During internal rotation, the occiput typically rotates anteriorly toward the maternal symphysis pubis to align with the widest part of the pelvic outlet. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T005#GNS226_U3_T005_h5)

question: What acts as the fulcrum (hypomochlion) during the extension of the fetal head?

options.B: The inferior margin of the symphysis pubis

explanation: The occiput pivots around the inferior border of the symphysis pubis, allowing the head to extend upward and outward over the perineum. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T005#GNS226_U3_T005_h6)

question: What is the primary nursing responsibility during the extension phase of labour?

options.A: Administering general anesthesia to stop contractions
options.B: Supporting the perineum and controlling the speed of head delivery
options.C: Performing an immediate routine episiotomy on all clients
options.D: Applying fundal pressure to hasten delivery

explanation: Nurses protect maternal tissue during extension by supporting the perineum and guiding the mother to push gently or pant to prevent rapid tearing. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T005#GNS226_U3_T005_h6)

question: What causes restitution of the fetal head immediately following its delivery?

options.A: The intentional manual rotation by the birth attendant
options.B: The untwisting of the neck as the head aligns back with the shoulders
options.C: The abrupt drop in maternal systemic blood pressure
options.D: The immediate contraction of the abdominal wall

explanation: Restitution is the passive untwisting of the fetal neck as the delivered head returns to its natural anatomical alignment with the shoulders. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T005#GNS226_U3_T005_h7)

question: What causes the subsequent movement of external rotation?

options.A: The internal rotation of the fetal shoulders within the pelvis
options.B: The relaxation of the uterine fundus
options.C: The stretching of the round ligaments
options.D: The active crying of the newborn

explanation: External rotation of the head is driven by the internal rotation of the shoulders as they adapt to the anteroposterior diameter of the pelvic outlet. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T005#GNS226_U3_T005_h7)

question: Which shoulder is typically delivered first during the expulsion phase?

options.D: Whichever shoulder is closest to the sacrum

explanation: The anterior shoulder is delivered first under the symphysis pubis, followed by the delivery of the posterior shoulder over the perineum. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T005#GNS226_U3_T005_h8)

question: What event immediately follows the complete expulsion of the fetus?

options.A: The transition to the third stage of labour (placental delivery)
options.B: The initiation of the first stage of labour
options.C: The surgical repair of the cervix
options.D: The immediate administration of general anesthesia

explanation: Expulsion of the fetus marks the conclusion of the second stage and transitions the patient into the third stage of labour, focused on placental separation. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T005#GNS226_U3_T005_h8)
